note: Written by hand from the runs of tests/unit/test_erasure_reach.py, test_erasure_reach_restore.py and test_erasure_reach_tool.py; each shown finding is held by a strict xfail, a variant case or reach.json.

findings.expected: No owed entry for a store inside the box (plan 8 section 3, criterion 8)
findings.claim: The erasure registry owes erasure in 27 stores, 26 of them inside the box
findings.owning_lane: B2 (with C2, A2, E, D for their rows)

findings.expected: After an opt-out the pseudonym is in no store or snapshot (criterion 8)
findings.claim: The lake's kept snapshot, Parquet and NDJSON keep the opted-out patient with the note's name, chart number and phone; the embed cache keeps the vectors of the patient's chunks. Ruled by D-513 and D-862 (the owner's ruling); plan 8 criterion 8 now asks for more
findings.evidence: the lake:db, lake:parquet, lake:ndjson and lake:embed_cache.duckdb cases of tests/unit/test_erasure_reach.py

findings.claim: omop.tb_record_event keeps the before-images, the note's name, chart number and phone among them. Ruled by D-1031 (the owner's ruling); plan 8 criterion 8 now asks for more
A job's list, a per-patient file and an attached chart of the patient stay in the object store. Ruled by D-513 (the owner's ruling); plan 8 criterion 8 now asks for more
trace.traces keeps a model call's body with the pseudonym and the name
pidmap.identity keeps the opted-out patient's encrypted identity
The recall tables keep the unsalted recall hash of the pseudonym. Ruled by the review of D-866 (left owed); plan 8 criterion 8 now asks for more

A CASE job's request (orch.jobs) and an EDC draft (edc.draft, erasure.py:383) keep the pseudonym. The draft is held by D-1032 (the owner's ruling) and its open question; plan 8 criterion 8 now asks for more

findings.expected: No log line names a patient (derived_store.py:730)
findings.claim: The derive batch's failure line names the pseudonym through the box's own JSON formatter (libs/tb_common/logging.py:132); the run's log text held it after the ticks

findings.expected: A restore re-applies the opt-out list (review J-2; plan 8 V7)
findings.claim: The register is re-applied, but the restored stores hold the patient until the worker's next tick, and a complete restore releases its hold before that tick

findings.expected: Every store has one registry entry (D-465)
findings.claim: 4 top-level lake entries are not in the registry: gates, night_runs.json, site_key.json, source.jsonl (none held the patient)

findings.expected: A test finds the pseudonym in no FHIR resource (criterion 8)
findings.claim: Not searched: the FHIR store, the backups, the provenance index, a practice space's stores and the vector store; the live mode exists and was not run on a compose box

findings.expected: The registry says what an opt-out keeps (D-465)
findings.claim: orch.submissions is an erase entry with a clear and the generated registry lists it as erased; a live submission of the patient stays, as D-513 (the owner's ruling) keeps it: the registry and the decision do not match
findings.evidence: the orch.submissions case; the variant 'orch.submissions: a live submission'

findings.claim: An uncertain mail of the patient's own file and a queued mail of a list (in the test, its body names the patient) keep their requests. Ruled by D-863 and D-874 (the integrator's rulings); plan 8 criterion 8 now asks for more
findings.evidence: the mail.send_keys case and its variants

findings.claim: A set-up sheet of many patients keeps the patient: its file, its row, its check items and its column examples. Ruled by D-869 (left owed); plan 8 criterion 8 now asks for more
findings.evidence: the sitesetup.input, sitesetup.check_item and sitesetup.fix cases and variants

findings.expected: Nothing of an opted-out patient stays (criterion 8)
findings.claim: The box keeps each service's log (json-file, 10 files of 100 MB) and nothing on the opt-out reaches it; the registry has no entry for logs
findings.evidence: read from the compose file, not run
